segments: Nobody is coming to save you.
Epictetus was born a slave. He said:

“First say to yourself what you would be;
and then do what you have to do.”
Discourses 3.23
Decide who you are. Then act like him.
Save this. Start Monday.
Your mind is turning into what you scroll.
Marcus Aurelius warned himself:

“The soul becomes dyed with
the colour of its thoughts.”
Meditations 5.16

Feed it better.
Books, hard work, good men.
Follow for one rule a day.
You can survive anything with one thing.

Nietzsche wrote it.
Viktor Frankl lived it in Auschwitz.

“He who has a why to live
can bear almost any how.”
Twilight of the Idols, Maxims 12
Find your why. The hows get lighter.
Send this to someone carrying a lot.
Tired. Broke. Nobody watching.
Doesn’t change the job.

“Just that you do the right thing.
The rest doesn’t matter.”
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 6.2

Cold or warm. Tired or rested.
Praised or ignored.
Save this for the days you want to quit.
Anyone can get angry. That’s easy.
Aristotle set a higher bar.
“To be angry with the right person, to the right degree, at the right time, for the right purpose, and in the right way: that is not easy.”
Nicomachean Ethics II.9
Anger isn’t the problem. Aim is.
Send this to a brother with a short fuse.

You don’t want responsibility?
Someone worse will take it.
Plato wrote the warning 2,400 years ago.
“The heaviest penalty for declining to rule is to be ruled by someone inferior to yourself.”
Republic, Book I

Step up at work. At home.
In your own life.
Follow for more.
Everything hit you at once this week.
Marcus Aurelius had the picture for it:
“Be like the headland on which the waves break. It stands firm, and the seething waters around it fall asleep.”
Meditations 4.49

You don’t have to stop the waves.
Just stand.
Save this for the next storm.

Everything that happens to you
has two handles.
Epictetus:
“Every thing has two handles, one by which it may be carried, the other by which it cannot.”
Enchiridion 43

Your brother wronged you?
Don’t grab ‘he wronged me’.
Grab ‘he’s my brother’.
Send this to someone holding a grudge.

You can fight your life
or you can walk with it.
Seneca quoted the old Stoic Cleanthes:

“Fate leads the willing
and drags the unwilling.”
Letter 107

Either way you’re going.
Choose to walk.
Save this.

They can take everything from you.
Except one thing.

Viktor Frankl learned this
in a concentration camp.
“The last of the human freedoms: to choose one’s attitude in any given set of circumstances.”
Man’s Search for Meaning

Nobody can take that.
Don’t hand it over.
Send this to someone who feels trapped.
Asking for help isn’t weak.
The emperor of Rome said so himself.
“Do not be ashamed to be helped. Like a soldier storming a wall, you have a job to do.”
Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 7.7

If you’re limping, lean on someone.
Then keep climbing.

Send this to a brother
who’s struggling in silence.

You don’t need a holiday.
You need this.
Marcus Aurelius:
“Nowhere can a man find a quieter or more untroubled retreat than in his own soul.”
Meditations 4.3

Ten quiet minutes. No phone.
Go there today.
Save this for when it gets loud.
You’re afraid your life will be short.
Seneca said you’re measuring the wrong thing.
“As with a play, so with life: what matters is not how long it is, but how well it is acted.”
Letter 77

Act well today.
That’s the whole job.
Follow for one rule a day.
They got away with it. You didn’t.
Socrates would tell you that you won.

“It is worse to do wrong
than to suffer wrong.”
Plato, Gorgias 469c

The man who cheats you damages himself.
Stay clean.
Send this to someone who got burned.
Injured. Sick. Broke. Still you.
Epictetus walked with a limp his whole life.
“Sickness is a hindrance to the body, but not to the will, unless the will itself chooses.”
Enchiridion 9

Your body can be stopped.
Your choices can’t.
Save this for the hard days.
You want the whole life fixed by Friday.

Marcus Aurelius built his
one action at a time.
“Build your life action by action, and be content if each one achieves its goal as far as it can.”
Meditations 8.32
One honest action. Then the next.
Follow for more.

You didn’t choose your family.
Or your city. Or your time.
Marcus Aurelius didn’t either. He wrote:
“Love the people fate has brought you together with, and do it with all your heart.”
Meditations 6.39

Stop wishing for a different hand.
Play this one with love.
Send this to the people you’re stuck with.
Something went wrong today. Good.
Epictetus had a drill for it:
“On every accident that befalls you, ask yourself what power you have for turning it to use.”
Enchiridion 10

Insulted? Patience. Pain? Endurance.
Loss? Freedom.
Save this for the next bad day.
You’re looking for it everywhere but here.
Marcus Aurelius pointed inward:
“Dig within. Within is the wellspring of good, and it will always flow if you keep digging.”
Meditations 7.59

The good man you’re looking for
is a decision away.
Follow for one rule a day.
